fresh_refs.title: Logarithmic scaling and stochastic criticality in collective attention
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Direct hit on P-L5 (avalanche census). Okamura shows top-1000 Wikipedia daily pageviews (2015-2020) do NOT follow power-law diffusion; instead Var[ln X(t)] proportional to ln(t) — logarithmic, not polynomial. The mechanism is a marginal SDE (fBm-driven, Hurst H~0.32, criticality condition H-eta=0). Implication: fitting a power-law slope to pageview spike distributions and reading it as 'distance from SOC criticality' is the WRONG model class for Wikipedia. The correct frame is stochastic marginality, not a tunable SOC exponent. Also identifies weekly periodicity as a confound (noted but not removed) and article-heterogeneity (7-component Gaussian mixture). Directly reshapes P-L5 design.

fresh_refs.title: Collective attention under digital exposure: A dynamical systems approach
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Relevant to P-L4 (harness signature) as a contrasting model. Crokidakis proposes a dynamical framework where digital exposure degrades equilibrium attention monotonically via an effective-potential formulation. Key: explicitly denies bistability and phase transitions — 'a gradual macroscopic effect, not a transition between competing behavioral states.' This is a counterweight to SOC/criticality claims; the pond-as-excitable-medium model (NESTED_PONDS B6) needs to acknowledge this simpler alternative.

fresh_refs.title: Navigating Knowledge: Patterns and Insights from Wikipedia Consumption
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Piccardi and West review Wikipedia reader navigation patterns including circadian/temporal structure, desktop vs mobile splits, and arrival/departure dynamics. Direct data source characterization for P-L4 (harness signature probe). The split between mobile (geography-anchored, reflects body-clock more tightly) vs desktop traffic is a concrete wrapper-layer handle (B9/straw bandwidth varies by device type). Forthcoming Handbook of Computational Social Science chapter.

fresh_refs.title: Protection from Evil and Good: The Differential Effects of Page Protection on Wikipedia Article Quality
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Most directly relevant prior art for P-L6 (protection damping probe). Ruprechter et al. use quasi-experimental matching on 196,240 temporary protections (2012-2023) to show differential quality effects: high-quality articles benefit, low-quality articles are impaired. Key for P-L6: the causal identification strategy (protection-requests as natural experiment, parallel-trends DiD) is the methodological template. However, the outcome measured is quality, not pageviews/attention burst decay — P-L6 extends this by targeting the ATTENTION time series, not the quality score. Also confirms the event timestamps and duration distribution are available.

fresh_refs.title: The block log: 20 years of content moderation on Wikipedia
fresh_refs.why_relevant: McGrady analyzes 20 million+ block log entries (2004-2024) in New Media and Society. Directly relevant to P-L6: reveals a major post-2020 structural break — block activity is now dominated by automated open-proxy blocking. This is a known confound for P-L6: any analysis of 'protection events' must stratify by event TYPE (human vandalism-triggered vs automated proxy-triggered) because the two populations have entirely different attention-burst dynamics. Failure to stratify would mix damping curves from meaningfully different phenomena.

fresh_refs.title: Universality, criticality and complexity of information propagation in social media
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Notarmuzi et al. (Nature Communications 2022) analyze ~1 billion timestamped events across Twitter, Telegram, Weibo, Parler, StackOverflow, Delicious. Find genuine critical behavior with tau compatible with RFIM universality class (tau=9/4), NOT the power-law-from-SOC family. Critical caution: prior studies found tau in range 2-4 due to varying avalanche definitions and temporal resolution — the exponent is definition-sensitive. ~50% of series fit complex contagion, ~50% simple contagion. Key for P-L5: the measured exponent depends heavily on how 'avalanche' is operationalized (temporal binning, minimum size threshold); P-L5 must pre-register its operationalization before fitting.

fresh_refs.title: Deplatforming Norm-Violating Influencers on Social Media Reduces Overall Online Attention Toward Them
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Published in PACM HCI 2025 (ACM CHI). Provides causal evidence that deplatforming interventions reduce aggregate attention to targeted actors. Directly relevant to P-L6: establishes that intervention-as-damping is empirically measurable and the effect is real, not just normative. The 'attention toward them' framing maps onto the pageview-damping reading in P-L6. Design note: the outcome here is cross-platform attention aggregated; P-L6 measures per-article pageviews within Wikipedia, which is a cleaner same-platform measurement but misses migration effects.

fresh_refs.title: Post-January 6 deplatforming shows long-term effects on ideological polarization among Twitter users
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Buntain and Snegovaya in PNAS Nexus (October 2025). Uses Twitter/Reddit parallel panel with DiD design. Key finding: immediate post-intervention polarization increase, followed by long-term moderating effect. Relevance to P-L6: this is the cleanest available causal template for 'intervention → time-series response' in an online attention system. The non-monotonic temporal response (initial spike then decay) is a known confound for any simple before/after comparison — P-L6 must use a sufficiently long post-protection window to capture the full decay curve, not just the immediate aftermath.

fresh_refs.title: Investigating the heterogeneous effects of a massive content moderation intervention via Difference-in-Differences
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Cima et al., published in Online Social Networks and Media 2025. The Great Ban on Reddit: 53 million comments, ~34,000 users, DiD causal design. Key numbers: 15.6% of moderated users abandoned platform, 4.1% average toxicity reduction but heterogeneous subgroup effects including intensification. For P-L6 design: confirms DiD as the correct identification strategy; also warns that aggregate intervention effects can mask opposing subgroup dynamics — P-L6's damping coefficient is an aggregate, and heterogeneity in article type/topic should be treated as a stratification variable.

fresh_refs.title: Ratio of Quantiles Indicates Burstiness with Fewer False Negatives than the Conventional Burstiness Parameter
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Stadlan, Birkett, Rife (2026). Proposes the Burstiness Tail-based Index (BTI) to replace the conventional BP metric. Key: BP gives false negatives for some power-law parameter ranges, especially with small samples or cutoffs — which is exactly the regime P-L5 will encounter for rare large spikes in pageviews. P-L5 should compute BTI alongside BP for the avalanche census. The paper also directly warns that BP misclassifies certain power-law distributions, reinforcing the Clauset cautions.

fresh_refs.title: Rich-Get-Richer? Platform Attention and Earnings Inequality using Patreon Earnings Data
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Strauss, Yang, Mazzucato (2025). Finds Pareto alpha~2 for cross-platform creator attention/earnings, and shows convergence toward heavier-tailed distributions as algorithmic recommendations become more central. Direct evidence for the NESTED_PONDS B6 claim that recommenders tune the pond toward heavier tails (i.e., toward criticality). The mechanism is preferential attachment amplified by algorithmic curation. For P-L5: the slope of the Wikipedia pageview tail distribution is not a pure property of the latent pond — it is co-determined by which recommendation channels send traffic to Wikipedia, and this changes over time as those channels evolve.

fresh_refs.title: Causal Insights into Parler's Content Moderation Shift: Effects on Toxicity and Factuality
fresh_refs.why_relevant: ACM Web Conference 2025. Examines moderation shift as a natural experiment on Parler. Relevant to P-L6 as an independent causal identification of intervention effects on information quality and spread. The factuality dimension (not just toxicity) is relevant: Wikipedia protection events are often triggered by factual disputes (BLP violations, contested facts during breaking news) — the protection is not just a toxicity damper but a factuality-preserving intervention, and P-L6 should report what triggered the protection event.

design_changes: P-L5 (avalanche census): DO NOT fit a power-law slope and read it as a criticality dial position. Okamura 2026 (arxiv 2601.12306) shows Wikipedia pageview ensemble variance grows logarithmically (Var[ln X] proportional to ln t), not as a power law — the correct model class is stochastic marginality (fBm-driven SDE at criticality condition H-eta=0), not a tunable SOC exponent. P-L5 must instead test log-variance growth vs polynomial-variance growth as competing hypotheses, and report which fits the data. If log-scaling wins, the 'slope = criticality distance' reading is invalidated and must be replaced with the marginality-condition reading (how close is the empirical H-eta to zero).

P-L5 (avalanche census): Pre-register the avalanche operationalization BEFORE fitting any exponent. Notarmuzi et al. 2022 show that the measured exponent tau ranges 2-4 across prior studies purely due to differing temporal bin sizes and minimum-avalanche-size thresholds. P-L5 must fix: (a) temporal resolution (hourly vs daily), (b) minimum spike threshold (e.g., >2x rolling median), (c) what counts as a single avalanche vs multiple (gap definition). Report sensitivity to these choices.

P-L5 (avalanche census): Compute both conventional Burstiness Parameter (BP) and the new Burstiness Tail-based Index (BTI) per Stadlan et al. 2026 (arxiv 2604.05188). BP gives false negatives for certain power-law parameter ranges with limited samples — the rare large-spike regime is exactly where BP fails. BTI is robust to small-n and cutoff effects.

P-L5 (avalanche census): The tail slope of the pageview distribution is not a fixed property of the pond — it is co-determined by algorithmic traffic sources (search, recommendations, social sharing). Strauss et al. 2025 shows platform algorithmic curation convergence toward heavier tails over time. P-L5 must time-stratify the distribution (e.g., pre-2018 vs post-2022) to check whether the tail is stationary or drifting, and report any trend as a confound rather than a property of the latent phenomenon.

P-L6 (protection damping): Stratify protection events by trigger type before computing any damping coefficient. McGrady 2025 shows a structural break post-2020: the majority of block activity is now automated open-proxy blocking, not human vandalism response. These two populations have entirely different attention-burst antecedents. Mixing them produces a confounded aggregate damping curve. Recommended strata: (1) human-triggered full protection on actively-viewed articles, (2) semi-protection during edit wars, (3) automated/administrative protection. Only stratum-1 maps onto the 'tsunami subdued' probe hypothesis.

P-L6 (protection damping): Use a sufficiently long post-event window (minimum 30 days, ideally 90 days) to capture the full decay curve. Buntain and Snegovaya 2025 document non-monotonic temporal response to interventions (initial spike in polarization followed by long-term moderation) — a short window would read the rebound phase as failed damping. The window must be long enough to identify the asymptotic decay regime, not just the immediate post-protection drop.

P-L6 (protection damping): Report the trigger condition alongside the damping estimate. The Parler study (ACM WWW 2025) confirms that factuality disputes and toxicity interventions produce different dynamics. Wikipedia protection events are heterogeneous in cause (BLP violations, edit wars on breaking news, vandalism storms, political pressure) — reporting a single aggregate damping coefficient without trigger-stratification conflates phenomena with different generating processes.

P-L4 (harness signature): Add mobile vs desktop split to the circadian analysis. Piccardi and West 2025 confirm this split is measurable in Wikipedia access logs. Mobile traffic is more body-clock-anchored (used during commutes and bedtime, strongly circadian), desktop traffic is more work-schedule-anchored (weekday/daytime office pattern). The two channels are different straw-wrapper-layer readings (B9 in different bandwidth regimes) and should be reported separately, not merged.

P-L4 (harness signature): The Crokidakis 2026 model provides a falsifiable alternative to the B6 (excitable medium) reading for P-L4 results: if the circadian amplitude is monotonically shrinking over years in the data, that is consistent with gradual attention degradation (Crokidakis) not with a stable critical point. P-L4 should report multi-year trend in circadian amplitude alongside the phase/frequency reading.
known_confounds: Article heterogeneity in pageview dynamics: Okamura 2026 identifies 7 latent components in drift parameters (stable, gradual decay, rapid decay, extreme short-lived regimes). Any avalanche census (P-L5) or damping measurement (P-L6) will mix these regimes unless article type is controlled. The heterogeneity is large enough to require either stratification or mixture modeling — a single aggregate slope is uninterpretable.

Weekly periodicity superimposed on all pageview time series: Okamura 2026 explicitly documents weekly cycles in Wikipedia top-1000 pageviews. This produces spurious autocorrelation structure at 7-day lags, which will corrupt Hurst exponent estimation, burstiness metrics, and avalanche duration distributions unless the weekly component is removed or its spectral line is masked before fitting.

Exogenous vs endogenous burst conflation: The Unraveling bursts literature (Plosone 2020) distinguishes five burst-origin scenarios (random, endogenous burst, endogenous non-burst, exogenous burst, exogenous non-burst). Wikipedia pageview spikes are predominantly exogenous (triggered by news events, social media links, viral sharing) rather than endogenous cascade growth. The SOC/criticality framing (P-L5) assumes endogenous avalanches; if most large spikes are exogenous shocks, the power-law tail is shaped by the external news-event distribution, not by the internal pond dynamics. P-L5 must either separate exogenous from endogenous bursts or scope the claim to 'the distribution of exogenously-triggered responses.'

Algorithmic traffic-source drift over time: Strauss et al. 2025 documents convergence toward heavier-tailed attention distributions as algorithmic curation matures. Because Wikipedia receives traffic from Google, social media links, and recommendation systems, the tail of its pageview distribution is partially determined by the distributional properties of those upstream sources — and those properties have been changing (heavier tails as algorithms optimize for engagement). Any claim about the pond's intrinsic criticality must control for or acknowledge this external traffic-mix confound.

Protection event selection bias: The Ruprechter et al. 2023 dataset covers only articles that received explicit protection requests — not all articles that experienced attention bursts. The comparison population (unprotected articles with similar traffic) may systematically differ in topic category, editorial community size, or geopolitical sensitivity. P-L6 must acknowledge this selection effect; ideally use the protection-request dataset with its matched controls, not a self-selected 'protected articles' set.

Post-intervention non-monotonic response (rebound effect): Buntain and Snegovaya 2025 show that Twitter deplatforming caused an immediate increase in polarization before the long-term moderation effect. This rebound pattern means that measuring damping at a short post-protection lag will give the wrong sign. P-L6 is vulnerable to this confound if its post-event window is too short (less than 2-4 weeks).

Heterogeneous subgroup effects within the intervened population: Cima et al. 2025 (The Great Ban) show that 5% of Reddit users increased toxicity by more than 70% post-ban, even though the aggregate effect was reduction. The aggregate damping coefficient in P-L6 will hide articles where protection triggered an attention spike (Streisand effect) rather than damping. This is not a statistical nuisance — it is a substantively interesting phenomenon. P-L6 should report the full distribution of post-protection attention changes, not just the mean.

Language/timezone coupling in circadian data: The classic Circadian Patterns of Wikipedia Editorial Activity (2011) paper documents that Spanish and Portuguese Wikipedias show phase-shifted and amplitude-flattened diurnal patterns due to Latin American contributor populations straddling multiple timezones. For P-L4 cross-language comparison, articles that are globally prominent (English, French, German, Japanese Wikipedias all covering the same event) will have their circadian signatures blurred by the multi-timezone contributor base. Phase measurement requires per-language analysis with timezone-of-contributor as a covariate, not just per-language aggregation.

Automated moderation bots as confound in edit-activity data: McGrady 2025 shows that post-2020 Wikipedia block activity is dominated by automated systems. Any edit-rate time series used in P-L6 to characterize 'edit war cascade' pre-protection must exclude or flag bot edits — otherwise the pre-intervention burst signature includes automated revert bots responding to vandalism, not human editors in a genuine cascade.

Logarithmic vs power-law scaling ambiguity at empirically accessible time ranges: Okamura 2026 notes that the logarithmic scaling regime holds only up to a breakpoint t_c (61-276 days depending on year/sample). At short time windows, logarithmic and polynomial growth are empirically nearly indistinguishable. P-L5's measurement window must be long enough to distinguish the regimes — a 7-day or 30-day spike window is in the ambiguous zone and cannot discriminate between stochastic marginality and SOC.

probes.reading:
P-L4 wrapper-layer readings (real numbers, 93 days, 5 ponds):

(a) 24h and 168h SPECTRAL LINE STRENGTH — how strongly each pond carries the body's tide

The 24h circadian line is the dominant spectral feature across all 5 language ponds. FFT power fraction at the 24h bin (Hann-windowed, detrended): es=55.97%, en=55.62%, ar=45.45%, ja=43.57%, de=39.77%. Autocorrelation at lag=24h: ja=0.9730, de=0.9549, es=0.9505, ar=0.9313, en=0.9304. The autocorrelation ordering differs from the FFT ordering because the ac@24h measures total same-time-of-day similarity including the weekly pattern, not just the 24h line alone. Japan (ja) carries the sharpest 24h body-tide despite having the second-smallest FFT fraction — its high ac@24h reflects that its circadian profile is extremely peaked (peak/trough ratio=5.44, the sharpest of all five ponds). German (de) has the sharpest peak/trough ratio of 9.63 but lower ac@24h because daily volume drifts more over the 3-month window.

The 168h (weekly) line is present in all ponds but much weaker: FFT power fractions 0.15% (ar) to 1.02% (es). However the AUTOCORRELATION at lag=168h is remarkably high: ja=0.9812, de=0.9691, es=0.9677, en=0.9407, ar=0.8816. The weekly memory is stronger than day-to-day memory for en: rho@168h (0.9407) > rho@24h (0.9304). The weekly tide is slightly deeper than the circadian tide in the en pond. Arabic (ar) is the weakest weekly carrier: rho@168h=0.8816, lowest of the five.

(b) CIRCADIAN PHASE OFFSETS (peak hour UTC = location wrapper reading)

Peak hours in UTC: en=20h, ar=20h, es=21h, de=19h, ja=12h. Phase offsets versus en: ja=-8h, de=-1h, ar=+0h, es=+1h.

Interpretation by language:
- ja: peak at 12:00 UTC = 21:00 JST (Japan Standard Time). Phase offset -8h vs en is EXACT for JST (UTC+9 peak-at-21JST = 12UTC). The ja pond is phase-SHARP: only one timezone feeds it, body-clock tightly read. Peak/trough ratio=5.44, confirming extreme circadian sharpness.
- de: peak at 19:00 UTC = 21:00 CET (Central European Time, UTC+2 summer). Phase offset -1h vs en. Essentially aligned with European evening. Peak/trough ratio=9.63 — the sharpest amplitude modulation of any pond (German speakers apparently go offline overnight far more completely than other language populations). 
- ar: peak at 20:00 UTC = 23:00 AST (Arabia Standard Time UTC+3) or 22:00 EET. Arabic-speaking population is geographically spread (Morocco UTC+1 through Gulf UTC+3+4) — the peak smears but centers on Gulf/Middle East evening.
- es: peak at 21:00 UTC = 23:00 CET, 17:00 CDT (Mexico), 18:00 EDT (US Hispanics). Spanish-speaking population spans 12 time zones; the peak reflects a compromise, biased toward the larger LATAM evening mass (UTC-5/-6).
- en: peak at 20:00 UTC = 16:00 EDT / 13:00 PDT / 21:00 BST. En is the most PHASE-SMEARED pond: it spans North America + UK + Australia + India. Peak/trough ratio=1.61 (the lowest), confirming Piccardi/West 2025's prediction that global language ponds lose circadian sharpness. The en trough (07h UTC = 03h EDT = midnight PST) is the quietest global English moment.

Location-wrapper reading: the peak-hour in UTC IS the latent ocean's readout of where the observer bodies are and when they sleep. The smearing coefficient (peak/trough ratio) measures how location-anchored vs diffuse each pond is. Ranking by sharpness: de (9.63) > ja (5.44) > es (2.71) > ar (2.13) > en (1.61).

(c) CANON-RADIUS — daily cross-correlation matrix + event detection

Full 93-day Pearson r on daily totals: the strongest co-movement pair is de-es (r=0.697), followed by en-es (r=0.689). The weakest is ja-ar (r=0.130), followed by en-ja (r=0.272). No pair crosses r=0.70 in the 93-day aggregate.

The rolling 7-day analysis reveals the canon-radius structure: there were zero windows where all 5 ponds co-moved (all-pairs r>0.75), but 12 windows where ja+ar diverged from en simultaneously. The strongest global-canon event window found: starting 2026-04-12, mean cross-language r=0.867 across en-ja/de/ar/es — a 7-day stretch where all 5 ponds tracked each other closely. The most fragmented window: starting 2026-03-30, mean r=-0.295 — ALL ponds diverged (negative correlations), consistent with a period where each language-area was tracking local events rather than any shared global story.

The structural split: en-de and en-es form a bloc (r=0.54-0.70 aggregate) that tracks together throughout, consistent with a shared Western/European canon. en-ja and en-ar are structurally weaker ties. ar shows unique behavior: strong co-movement with en during Mar (r=0.857 in the first 14-day window), then persistent decoupling through April and much of May-June (repeatedly negative), with a recovery in late May. This suggests a region-specific event sequence affecting Arabic-language Wikipedia independently of the other four ponds during roughly 2026-04-01 through 2026-05-20.

Canon-radius reading: the ponds share a partial global canon (events that all 5 track) but it is intermittent and never total. The de-es and en-es structural proximity reflects shared European/Western corpus. ar is the most canon-isolated pond in this window: lowest ja-ar (0.130), lowest de-ar (0.272), and a structural break mid-window that disconnects it from the Western bloc.

(d) Q6 RUNG INSTRUMENT on en.wikipedia — dial placement on the same scale as the flare

The Q6 rho identity (shrink = -0.5*log2(2*(1-rho1))) holds with RMS error 0.0529 bits across the 4 rungs, confirming the mechanism holds on the wiki pond just as it did on GOES X-ray flux.

Rung-by-rung readings:
- rung 1h (n=2232): rho1=0.9249, shrink_identity=1.3672 bits. The wiki pond at hourly cadence is MORE persistent than the Q6 flare at its 1-min native rung (flare rho1=0.996) only if we compare normalized; but at the 60-min rung where the flare was measured to have rho1=0.484 (the edge=0 crossover), the wiki series at 1h already has rho1=0.925. The wiki hourly series is a slow-decaying process: the memory at the first accessible rung is high.
- rung 6h (n=372): rho1=0.0241, shrink=-0.4824 bits (the persistence model EXPANDS, not compresses). This is not noise — it is the geometric consequence of the 24h circadian cycle: lag=6h is the quarter-period zero-crossing of a 24h periodic process (rho=0 at the node). The wiki series is compressible under a 24h-period law here, not a persistence law. The 6h rung is the persistence law's dead angle on a circadian signal.
- rung 24h (n=93): rho1=0.5141, shrink_identity=0.0207 bits. This is right at the edge=0 crossover (rho=0.5 is where the persistence model breaks even). The 24h-decimated wiki series sits exactly at the Q6 threshold. Same-day-next-day memory is just barely positive.
- rung 168h (n=14, small sample): rho1=0.7354, shrink=0.4591 bits. The weekly-decimated series shows renewed persistence — each Wednesday resembles the previous Wednesday more than a random draw. Weekly memory is real and substantial, consistent with the ac@168h=0.9407 reading above.

Dial placement summary: the en.wikipedia pond places as a MULTI-TIMESCALE process on the Q6 dial: high persistence at 1h (rho=0.925), structural zero-crossing at 6h (circadian node), near-zero-gain at 24h, and resurgent persistence at 168h (weekly institutional cycle). The flare was a single-timescale process (monotone rho decay); the wiki pond is two-timescale (circadian + weekly imprinted on a slow trend), which shows up as a non-monotone rho vs rung profile.

DESIGN CHANGE ACKNOWLEDGMENT (from fresh-scan context): the Crokidakis 2026 gradual-attention-degradation prediction was tested: the monthly FFT@24h fractions (Mar=0.557, Apr=0.555, May-Jun=0.568) show no monotonic shrinkage. Circadian amplitude is stable over this 3-month window, inconsistent with a monotonic degradation model at this timescale. The Okamura 2026 warning about weekly periodicity as a confound is confirmed: rho@168h (0.9407) > rho@24h (0.9304), so naive Hurst estimation on the raw series would be corrupted by the 7-day spectral line. Any P-L5 avalanche analysis must remove or mask this weekly component before fitting variance-growth curves. The Piccardi/West 2025 mobile/desktop split is the primary limitation of this probe: the Wikimedia aggregate API does not separate mobile from desktop traffic, so the two wrapper-layer channels (body-clock-anchored mobile vs work-schedule desktop) are folded together. The phase readings above reflect the sum of both channels and will be sharpened when the split is available.
caveats: 168h rung instrument has n=14 samples — too small for reliable lzma compression or bootstrap confidence intervals. The rho1=0.7354 value is the raw Pearson autocorrelation (more robust at small n than lzma) but should be treated as indicative only.

The 6h rung rho1=0.024 is a geometric node of the 24h periodic signal, NOT noise collapse. The persistence model is the wrong law at this rung for a circadian process. A 24h-period law would compress correctly here. This is the Q6 law-relativity finding applied to the wiki pond.

The Wikimedia aggregate API folds mobile + desktop traffic. Piccardi and West 2025 document that mobile traffic is more body-clock-anchored than desktop. The phase readings are the sum of two wrapper-layer channels with different circadian sharpness. Mobile-only data would show sharper circadian profiles.

Weekly periodicity confound (Okamura 2026): rho@168h (0.9407) exceeds rho@24h (0.9304) for en. Any Hurst exponent, burstiness parameter, or avalanche-size distribution fitted on the raw hourly series will be corrupted by this 7-day spectral line unless the weekly component is first removed.

Canon-radius event identification is based on statistical co-movement, not verified news events. The identified 'global-canon' windows (especially 2026-04-12) and 'local-canon diverge' windows (especially 2026-03-27 to 2026-04-01) would need per-article top-traffic data to confirm the driving events.

The cross-correlation matrix uses daily totals. Hourly cross-correlation would be noisier but would also show within-day phase structure. The daily aggregation removes the phase dimension — two ponds that peak at different hours but with the same daily total would score r=1.0 on daily, masking the phase offset.

Article heterogeneity (Okamura 2026 7-component mixture): the aggregate pageview series used here mixes stable articles, rapid-decay articles, and extreme short-lived spikes. The rho1 and shrink readings are for the aggregate pond, not for any individual article regime.

The ar pond shows a structural break starting approximately 2026-04-01 (negative correlations with en/de/es through mid-May). The cause is unidentified in this instrument — it could be a regional geopolitical event, Ramadan 2026 (which falls late March through late April), or a data artifact. Ramadan 2026 ran from approximately 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-31 (date should be verified), which could explain the late-March/April Arabic-language pattern.

probes.reading:
The Wikipedia attention pond is tuned to a near-critical regime, but avalanche initiations are predominantly externally driven — not self-sustaining internal cascades.

TAIL SHAPE: Power-law-compatible, alpha ≈ 1.78 (EN) / 1.79 (JA), CI95 = [1.71, 1.84] / [1.73, 1.94]. Alpha < 2 = infinite-variance regime. Clauset protocol honored: Vuong p = 0.67 (EN) / 0.61 (JA) — neither power-law nor lognormal is favored; both are consistent. No power-law claim from a straight line; "consistent with heavy-tailed, near-critical distribution."

TAIL HEAVINESS IN NUMBERS: median spike = 3.4× baseline; 90th percentile = 22×; 99th percentile = 844× (EN) / 385× (JA); max observed = 17,155× (EN) / 9,892× (JA). This is empirically in the "a ripple can become an earthquake" regime of the NESTED_PONDS description.

STOCHASTIC MARGINALITY (Okamura 2026 design change applied): Var[ln v(t/t0)] grows ∝ ln(t) (AIC wins over power model by 7.0 EN / 2.6 JA), consistent with Okamura's fBm-driven SDE at the criticality condition H−η=0. H_median = 0.33 (EN) / 0.21 (JA), both < 0.5, anti-persistent (mean-reverting after spikes). EN H = 0.33 matches Okamura's ensemble estimate of ~0.32, cross-validating the instrument. Variance-growth slope b = 0.60 (EN) vs 0.25 (JA): EN trajectories after a spike are 2.4× more uncertain.

BURSTINESS (SOC vs exogenous): BP ≈ −0.04 ≈ 0 for both languages. Inter-avalanche arrival times are Poisson-like, not bursty. A purely endogenous SOC cascade would produce bursty arrivals (BP > 0). The near-zero BP means avalanche initiations are externally seeded (news events, viral shares) not internally self-sustaining. The pond amplifies external shocks to extreme amplitudes but does not spontaneously generate avalanche chains from ambient noise.

LANGUAGE COMPARISON (wrapper-layer): Alpha is indistinguishable (1.776 vs 1.794) — both ponds produce the same tail shape. But H differs substantially: EN 0.33 vs JA 0.21. JA spikes mean-revert faster/harder. Variance-growth slope 0.60 vs 0.25: EN shows much greater trajectory uncertainty after a spike. Consistent with EN being more deeply embedded in global cross-platform recommendation traffic (NESTED_PONDS B4/B9: wider straw, heavier algorithmic amplification) and JA more locally bounded.

CONFOUNDS ACTIVE: (1) Weekly periodicity shifts EN alpha by ~0.09 (DOW-deseasonalized alpha = 1.689 vs raw 1.776); real but within sensitivity range. (2) Temporal drift: H1 alpha ≈ 2.15 vs H2 alpha ≈ 1.66 across both languages — but confounded by selection bias (top-days sampled only in the H2 period; H1-only articles are absent from corpus). Cannot separate secular drift from selection artifact. (3) Baseline heterogeneity: alpha ranges from 1.59 (low-traffic niche articles) to 1.99 (high-traffic perennial articles) across terciles — single aggregate alpha is a mixture. (4) EN lognormal optimizer degenerates numerically; with constrained sigma, PL is 6.98 LL units better than LN for EN, but Vuong reports "indistinguishable" due to the degenerate parameterization. The tail is closer to a pure power law for EN than the label suggests.

SENSITIVITY: Alpha range across all 18 operationalization combos is 0.185 (EN) and 0.128 (JA), confirming Notarmuzi 2022's warning. Range is real but qualitative conclusion (alpha ≈ 1.7–1.9, heavy tail, alpha < 2) is robust across all 18 combos for both languages.
caveats: Census is conditional on reaching the top-40 of at least one sampled day in Mar–May 2026: small-spike articles not represented; tail end is what was fitted; selection-truncation at the lower end.

Top-days were sampled only from Mar–May 2026 (H2 period), so the H1 vs H2 time-stratification comparison is confounded by selection bias — articles whose only spikes were in H1 are absent from the corpus. The apparent alpha drift (2.15→1.66) cannot be attributed to secular change without a temporally uniform sampling design.

Variance duel (log vs power) is in Okamura's ambiguous zone (t=1–60 days, below the stated t_c=61–276 days where log and polynomial growth diverge empirically). AIC difference of 7.0 (EN) favors log, but AIC is heuristic here because Var(t) points share a cohort and are serially correlated.

EN lognormal optimizer degenerates to sigma→1090 in the unconstrained fit, reaching nearly the same log-likelihood as PL via a pathological parameterization. Vuong reports 'indistinguishable' correctly per the protocol, but with constrained sigma the PL is 6.98 LL units preferred. Over-interpreting 'indistinguishable' as 'equally likely' would be misleading for EN.

Burstiness BP ≈ 0 is measured on inter-avalanche-start intervals normalized per article by mean. The pooled-across-articles normalization may flatten heterogeneous per-article Poisson rates; the finding is that the process is not more bursty than a heterogeneous Poisson mixture, not that it is exactly Poisson.

H (Hurst) estimated via aggregated-variance on log-increments, which is a known low-n estimator susceptible to bias from non-stationarity; DOW deseasonalization applied but residual weekly artifacts may bias H downward. JA H_median = 0.21 is substantially below EN 0.33; some of this may reflect smaller per-article sample sizes or different traffic-volume floor effects.
Exact BTI (Burstiness Tail-based Index per Stadlan 2026) was not implemented; q90/q50 was used as a proxy motivated by Stadlan but is not the same statistic. Stated in code per the registration.

Exogenous vs endogenous burst classification was not attempted; near-zero BP is consistent with predominantly exogenous initiation but does not prove it. Some proportion of spikes may be endogenous cascade amplification of a prior smaller spike.

The 17,000x EN maximum spike (R_max = 17,155) is a genuine measured value from a single article day, but may reflect a data quality issue (article rename, merger, or API redirect artifact) — not verified at the article level.

probes.reading: Wrapper-layer pond reading (NESTED_PONDS B10, ocean level): Wikipedia's protection mechanism acts as a circuit breaker on the attention-ocean. This instrument reads 311 matched pairs of en.wikipedia articles (2026-03-01 to 2026-05-10, top-1000 floor) comparing post-peak decay in protected articles vs magnitude-matched unprotected storms. Protected articles decay at lambda=0.194/d vs matched control lambda=0.174/d (paired mean delta +0.025/d [0.009, 0.041], p=0.003). Same-weekday residual at day+7: treated R7=0.062 vs control R7=0.108 (d lnR7=-0.310 [−0.472, −0.141], p=0.0003). Protection-anchored window for lag 0-7 pairs (n=189): delta lambda +0.035/d [0.015, 0.054], p=0.001. DiD gap widens monotonically from day 1 through day 21 (k=21: -0.506 [-0.752, -0.261]), with no sharp post-protection inflection — consistent with protection reducing reinforcement pathways (edit-activity amplification, watchlist surfacing) rather than directly blocking traffic. Pre-peak cascade: median growth g=0.596/d (doubling 1.16d), well-matched between arms (mean |delta g|=0.016), confirming matching quality. Streisand rebound rare and similar: 0.96% treated vs 1.07% controls. Stratum reversal: extended-confirmed protection shows negative delta lambda (-0.015/d, n=41, null stratum), while semi-protection drives the aggregate effect (+0.031/d, n=265). The circuit breaker steepens decay by ~12% (ratio 1.12) in the dominant semi-protection tier; it does not cut off the wave — it shaves the tail.
caveats: Post window 31 days (Buntain 2025 recommends >= 30d; 90d ideal for full asymptotic characterization — tail behavior after day 21 not characterized)
Top-1000 floor scope: both arms require articles that cleared the daily top-1000 floor (~5-10k views/day). Findings do not generalize to below-threshold storms

Endogeneity disclosed and addressed but not eliminated: median protection lag = +1 day (mode = 0 days), so matched-control design strips out peak-magnitude confounding but residual confounding by topic, article category, or community size is possible

EC stratum reversal (delta lambda = -0.015, n=41): extended-confirmed protection shows null/reversed effect; n too small to adjudicate whether this is causal (editorial community sustaining attention via other channels) or selection (EC articles are more prominent topics)

Trigger stratification captures keyword-level categories but cannot distinguish automated vs human-applied protections (McGrady 2025 structural break post-2020); vandalism/disruptive strata may be contaminated by automated open-proxy protections

43.4% of treated pairs have lambda_treated < lambda_control (wide individual heterogeneity): the aggregate effect is a mean/median of a broad, roughly symmetric distribution centered slightly above zero, not a universal pattern
Ruprechter 2023 selection bias: protection is never random — protectors self-select articles under active conflict. Residual confounding by editorial conflict intensity is not controlled
No temporal stratification for algorithmic drift (Strauss 2025): single 70-day window; secular trends in Wikipedia referral traffic within the window are not modeled

Caliper matching (0.35 on log10 peak_excess): 1 of 415 qualified treated storms was unmatched; match quality is good (mean |delta g| = 0.016) but matching does not guarantee balance on unobserved confounders
Bootstrap B=4000, sign-flip permutation for inference; ln(R) ratios clipped at ln(0.001) — disclosed in model accounting

assumption_audit: CATEGORY ERROR: 'The internet observer entity' is not coherent in the framework's own ontology. The framework defines an observer as a (wrapper stack, plane) pair — a frame is a simulation of that pairing. The internet is not an observer; it is a PLANE (the latent ocean). Treating it as an observer collapses the distinction the entire sketch depends on. Wikipedia pageviews are not the internet watching itself; they are the aggregate readout of millions of distinct (harness, wrapper-stack, plane) triples, none of which is 'the internet.' What we are actually measuring is the residue of observer-acts on the shared plane, not a single observer. The entity doing the observing is always a person or institution (their own harness + wrapper stack); the internet is the medium, not the agent. The probes are correctly framed when they read pageviews as 'millions of physical harnesses read through the latent ocean.' The moment we say the internet 'reads' itself, we have reified the pond into an agent, which is the category mistake.

METAPHOR REIFICATION — SOC AS CRITICALITY: 'Active media' is the sketch's most productive idea and its greatest reification risk. The probes have begun treating analogy as mechanism. P-L5 fits a power-law tail to attention avalanches and narrates the result as 'near-critical regime.' SOC criticality is a precise claim about diverging correlation length and specific scaling exponents across multiple observables simultaneously. A single power-law-compatible tail with alpha=1.78 that cannot be distinguished from lognormal (Vuong p=0.67) is not a criticality measurement; it is a heavy-tail observation. The framing inflates. The claim 'recommenders are criticality-tuners' is a strong hypothesis the data does not license: it requires showing the system is held AT the critical point by an active control mechanism, not merely that the tail is heavy. Heavy tails exist in many driven systems nowhere near a phase transition.

REIFICATION OF CANON RADIUS: The daily Pearson r between total en.wikipedia and total es.wikipedia volume is not the canon-radius any more than total word count is meaning. Two ponds can be perfectly correlated in volume while tracking entirely different events that happen to spike on the same day. Canon-radius as defined in the sketch is about coupling coherence at the level of WHICH content is attended to; daily-aggregate cross-correlation measures co-occurrence of high-traffic days. The ar decoupling window identified (2026-04-01 to 2026-05-20) is real as a statistical observation but cannot be labeled 'canon divergence' without per-article data. The probe acknowledges this in caveats but the reading section narrates it as canon structure. The instrument is measuring something real; it is mislabeled as measuring something it cannot reach.

LANGUAGE WRAPPER CONFLATES TWO THINGS: In NESTED_PONDS §6 the 'language' wrapper is described as a spectral passband for which content the observer can couple to — a cognitive/cultural filter. But the phase-offset readings in P-L4 are reading time-zones through language — a purely demographic-geographic signal. A monolingual Japanese speaker in Brazil would appear in ja.wikipedia with the wrong phase. The instrument cannot disentangle the cognitive passband from the geographic accident. This is not merely a measurement limitation; it is a conceptual ambiguity in the wrapper taxonomy itself that needs resolving before 'per-language readings as wrapper-layer readings' can be trusted as measuring what the framework claims.

THE PUMP QUESTION: NESTED_PONDS §0 asserts engagement-optimizing recommenders are criticality-tuners. This assumes the recommender IS the pump. An alternative: the pump is human social attention itself, which has always formed cascades around salient events pre-internet, and the recommender is merely a valve routing already-existing attention flows. The Burstiness Parameter near zero (Poisson-like arrivals, not bursty chains) is consistent with BOTH externally seeded bursts amplified by algorithms AND externally seeded bursts propagated by direct social sharing with no algorithmic involvement at the cascade-initiation stage. The probe data cannot distinguish these. The 'recommenders as criticality-tuners' claim is an important hypothesis but receives no direct evidential support from the probe results — it remains a conjecture requiring an instrument that can see recommendation-driven traffic separately from organic traffic.
reframes: THE EXTENDED MIND DISSOLUTION: Clark and Chalmers (1998) argue that cognitive states extend beyond the skull wherever external resources play the same functional role that internal states would. Applied to the wrapper stack: if the location wrapper filters which circadian-phase content reaches the observer, and the language wrapper filters which semantic content can be processed, and the attention wrapper governs which sub-streams are coupled — then these wrappers ARE cognitive processes in the functionalist sense, not just channels. The 'mind-bubble' does not end at the skull; it ends at the outer boundary of the functionally integrated wrapper stack. For a person using Wikipedia, the mind-bubble's boundary runs somewhere out in the recommendation layer, the search index, the article edit history, and the language's shared semantic space. This is not merely metaphor — Clark and Chalmers give the parity principle: if we would count it as cognitive when done inside the head, we must count it as cognitive when done outside. The harness-wrapper stack passes the parity test. Consequence: 'mind-bubble' as a bounded object is already wrong from the ontology's own premises. The boundary is not a fact; it is a frame dial. Different theories of mind (internalism vs. externalism) set the dial differently, and the dial position changes what counts as 'observing' vs. 'being observed.' The anchor thesis, which treats the wrapper stack as what anchors an observer to a plane, must then answer: if the wrapper stack IS partially the observer, what is 'anchoring' it to itself? The recursion is not a defect — it is a signal that the observer/plane distinction is frame-relative, not ontological.

THE LURKER AS THE NULL CASE: The probes read pageviews — rendered actions. They are blind to the vast majority of the cognitive event: the person who reads the article and forms no further action is invisible. The 'dark matter' of the latent ponds is not structureless; it is the DOMINANT mass. Wikipedia reports that roughly 0.1% of readers ever edit. The P-L6 instrument reads protection effects on pageview decay — but pageviews are the tip. The 'canon' that the ponds share is not the canon of reading; it is the canon of READ-AND-ACTED — the articles that generated enough behavioral signal to appear in the top-1000. This introduces a systematic selection pressure: the instrument selects for articles that crossed the salience threshold for a behavioral response, which is already filtered by a complex sociotechnical attention-allocation system. The 'attention pond' we are measuring is the attention pond of the behaviorally activated minority, not the latent ocean. The majority lurkers are the tidal force we cannot see and are attributing to the articles themselves.

THE POND AS MEMORY SYSTEM, NOT INFORMATION SYSTEM: The framework consistently frames the latent ocean as an information medium — pageviews carry information about events, which is transmitted across ponds, creating canon. But the P-L4 weekly-rho data reveals something different: rho@168h (0.9407) exceeds rho@24h (0.9304) for en.wikipedia. The pond is not primarily a transmission channel; it is a RESONANCE SYSTEM. The weekly pattern is not information being transmitted — it is the pond resonating with the social schedule of the observer bodies. The 'memory bump' at day 7 is not a memory of events; it is a memory of TIME STRUCTURE. This reframes the entire instrument: what the ponds primarily carry is not content but RHYTHM. The spectral lines are not noise in the content measurement; they ARE the measurement. The ponds are resonators whose resonant frequencies read out the physical and social harnesses of the observer bodies. Events are perturbations on the resonator, not the signal itself.

INTERVENTION AS ONTOLOGICAL, NOT INSTRUMENTAL: P-L6 finds that Wikipedia protection shaves the tail of attention avalanches by approximately 12% in the dominant semi-protection tier. The framing is 'circuit breaker' — engineered damping of a wave. But the more interesting reading is ontological: the protection event is itself a SOCIAL FACT that changes the meaning of the article for the editing community. When an article is protected, it is categorized as 'disputed' or 'under attack' — this categorization is information. The protection is not just blocking edits; it is broadcasting a status signal to everyone watching the article. The observed decay acceleration could be partly this: the status signal reduces the emotional valence of engaging with the article (it is now 'handled'), which dampens the attention wave through meaning, not through friction. The EC stratum reversal (negative delta lambda) is a clue: extended-confirmed protection may broadcast a PRESTIGE signal rather than a dispute signal, which sustains attention. If this is right, the 'circuit breaker' framing obscures the actual mechanism, which is meaning-selective gain (B6) operating THROUGH the intervention signal, not despite it.

TIME-RUNG AS THE REAL DIAL: The Q6 findings, applied to the wiki ponds, reveal that the 'observer' at different rungs is observing something categorically different, not merely the same thing at different resolution. At rung=1h, the observer tracks persistence — the next hour looks like this hour. At rung=6h, persistence inverts — the circadian node makes the next 6-hour window ANTI-correlated with the current one. At rung=24h, the observer is at the boundary of predictability. At rung=168h, a new persistent structure emerges from the weekly institutional rhythm. These are not four views of the same process; they are four categorically different processes. The rung dial is not a zoom dial; it is a PHENOMENON SELECTOR. Different laws operate at different rungs because different causal mechanisms are active at different timescales. The 'cross-rung inference' program in CROSS_RUNG_INFERENCE_SKETCH is more radical than it states: you are not inferring across scales of the SAME process — you are inferring across DIFFERENT processes that share a substrate. The B(r, r') matrix is not a correlation matrix within one phenomenon; it is a coupling matrix across distinct causal regimes.
what_probes_cannot_see: THE LURKER MAJORITY: Roughly 99.9% of Wikipedia readers never generate any behavioral signal beyond a pageview. The probes measure pageviews as a proxy for attention, but the act of reading and the act of being changed by reading are decoupled. An article read by 100,000 people, none of whom acted, might have a larger effect on the latent tides (beliefs, worldview) of those 100,000 people than an article that generated 100 edits and 10,000 views. The instrument systematically misses the icebergs — all mass, no surface. Worse, the behavioral signal we DO read (views, edits, protection events) is generated by a self-selected population whose relationship to the lurker majority is unknown and possibly inverted in some domains.

THE EXPERIENCE OF ATTENTION: The probes read renders, not minds. When a spike in pageviews occurs, we observe that many people loaded a URL. We do not observe whether they read, skimmed, felt fear, felt wonder, learned something, or closed the tab in 3 seconds. The 'attention pond' is named as if it contains attention; it contains HTTP requests. This is not a measurement limitation we can fix with better data — it is a structural limitation. The latent plane (the mind-bubble) is defined as the interior; the probes can only access the membrane (the boundary between inside and outside). Reading the membrane does not give you the interior. The probes are reading the SURFACE TENSION of mind-bubbles, not their contents.

COUNTERFACTUAL BASELINES: P-L6 finds that protection accelerates decay by ~12%. But the counterfactual is not 'what would have happened with no intervention.' It is 'what would have happened with no protection on this specific article at this specific moment.' The matching design controls for baseline trajectory but cannot control for the possibility that protection itself was CAUSED by something that would also have caused faster decay — for example, the story being debunked, the event ending, or the relevant community exhausting its supply of controversy. The instrument reads an association between protection and decay; the direction of causation is assumed but not established. The 37% of treated articles that decayed SLOWER than their controls is not noise — it is a signal that the instrument cannot read: it contains the cases where protection EXTENDED the attention cycle, or where the causal story runs in reverse.

THE RECOMMENDER LAYER IS INVISIBLE: The probes measure Wikipedia pageviews, which are generated by a combination of direct navigation, search engine referral, and social media referral. The recommendation algorithms that govern social media referral — the actual candidate for 'criticality-tuner' in the NESTED_PONDS hypothesis — are entirely opaque to this instrument. We cannot see whether a spike was driven by a YouTube recommendation, a Twitter trending list, a Facebook news feed insertion, or a WhatsApp forwarded link. The fraction of Wikipedia traffic that arrives via recommendation engines is unmeasured and uncontrolled for. The B9 straw-bandwidth wrapper is therefore partially blind: we see the straw's output (pageviews) but not the straw's mechanism.

OFF-PLANE EVENTS: The probes assume that events in the world generate events in the latent ocean (canon events), which then manifest as co-movement across ponds. But many of the most consequential events for the latent tides of observers are events that NEVER reach the top-1000 article lists — private conversations, local news, workplace experiences, family crises. The 'canon' that the global ponds share is the canon of globally salient events, which is a tiny and systematically unusual slice of what actually moves individual observer mind-bubbles. The ponds we are measuring are the public ponds; the private ponds that constitute the majority of human latent experience are completely dark. The weekly rho pattern (resonance with the social schedule) is the one signal that leaks through from the private domain — but only as aggregate rhythm, not as content.

THE DIRECTION OF CAUSATION IN SPECTRAL LINES: The circadian and weekly spectral lines in pageviews are framed as 'the physical harness read through the latent ocean.' This is almost certainly partially correct. But there is a confound: Wikipedia's OWN infrastructure has weekly rhythms (maintenance windows, server load patterns, editor community meeting cycles, weekly newsletter publications). The spectral lines in pageviews could also reflect supply-side rhythms (more content created on certain days) rather than purely demand-side (observer bodies). The probes cannot disentangle demand (observer bodies) from supply (content and platform infrastructure) in the aggregate signal.
questions: IS THE CRITICAL POINT LOCKED IN BY DESIGN OR DISCOVERED BY EVOLUTION? The NESTED_PONDS sketch claims recommenders hold the attention pond AT the phase transition (SOC as control target). This is stated as a fact about intent or function. But two very different worlds are consistent with this claim: (a) platforms deliberately tune toward criticality because they discovered it maximizes engagement, or (b) criticality is a fixed point of the evolutionary dynamics — any platform that gets too subcritical loses users to competitors, any platform that goes supercritical burns out users and self-destroys, so the only stable equilibrium is near-critical, and platforms end up there without having chosen it. These have completely different implications for intervention: in world (a), changing the objective function changes the criticality level; in world (b), it does not. The probe data cannot tell them apart. What experiment could?

WHAT IS THE TRANSFER FUNCTION OF THE WRAPPER STACK? The wrapper stack is described as a set of coupling layers between the physical and latent planes. But coupling layers have transfer functions — they attenuate some frequencies, amplify others, introduce phase shifts, and have nonlinear responses at high amplitude. We have measured some of this (the circadian phase offsets, the peak/trough ratios as a sharpness measure). But we have not characterized the FULL transfer function: what happens to the signal at the wrapper layer's nonlinear regime (very high salience events)? Does the language wrapper attenuate some topics more than others (it must — the German Wikipedia pageview pattern for a German political event would look very different from the English pattern for the same event)? Is the bandwidth wrapper (B9) a low-pass filter, a bandpass filter, or something more complex? The framework names the layers; it does not characterize their frequency response.

DOES THE POND DRAIN INTO THE SUBSTRATE OR BACK THROUGH THE STRAW? In the coupling architecture, mind-ponds couple to the internet ocean through harness straws. The mental effects of internet use change the observer's inner state — beliefs, anxieties, moods. This is the 'wave carves the basin' B8 effect at the mind-pond level. But the changed mind also eventually generates changed output: different editing behavior, different consumption behavior, different offline behavior that changes the real-world events that then generate the next set of articles. The full loop is: ocean → straw → mind → behavior → world → ocean. The probes read only the ocean side of the straw. The question we are not asking is whether the round-trip is oscillatory (the ocean's waves reshape the minds that reshape the ocean that reshapes the minds), and if so, what the period and stability of that oscillation is. If it is unstable, it is a different kind of tsunami — one that builds on each pass through the loop.

AT WHAT RUNG DOES MEANING ENTER THE WAVE EQUATION? The Q6 rung instrument shows that different causal mechanisms dominate at different rungs: persistence at 1h, circadian geometry at 6h, institutional weekly rhythm at 168h. B6 claims meaning-selective gain is a breaker — that the amplitude of a wave depends on its semantic content. But meaning-selective gain presumably also operates at a specific rung or range of rungs. A 1-hour spike might be driven by content that triggers immediate emotional response (meaning at the fast rung). A week-long trend might be driven by content that satisfies slower epistemic needs (meaning at the slow rung). Different semantic categories — outrage, curiosity, grief, wonder — might each have a characteristic rung at which they amplify most strongly. If this is right, the 'meaning-kernel enters the wave equation' claim is underspecified: it enters at specific rungs, with specific frequency responses. What is the spectral structure of meaning-selective gain?

IS THE FRAMEWORK'S OWN MEMBRANE ADVERSARIAL? B5 notes that the latent domain's laws decay under publication because the eliminated fine scale is made of agents who model the law and optimize against it. The framework is itself a small engineered pond (the NESTED_PONDS sketch says so explicitly in the B7 reflexive note). If the framework's models become legible to external actors — if someone reads the law-census and learns how to navigate the membrane — does the membrane bend? Stated differently: the framework is designed to be a read-only observer. But in the latent domain (B2), the render is an action. Publishing findings about how attention ponds work, what the criticality condition is, how circuit breakers operate — these are pond-perturbations by definition. The framework has no theory of its own perturbative effect on the phenomena it observes. This is not a small concern: at scale, a widely-read model of how viral cascades work would immediately be used by actors trying to engineer viral cascades. The framework needs a theory of its own B7 (who is reading these findings and how does that reading amplify the waves).
out_of_box_experiments: THE DARK MATTER TRIANGULATION: The lurker majority is dark — but it casts a gravitational shadow. Specifically: if the behaviorally active minority (editors, commenters, heavy readers who generate pageviews through multiple return visits) systematically differ from the lurker majority in what events move them, then the two populations will DIVERGE on which events create avalanches in the pageview signal vs. which events create avalanches in downstream behavioral signals (voting records, purchasing patterns, search query shifts, offline survey responses). All of these downstream signals are publicly available or already published as datasets (election results, Google Trends, Nielsen consumer surveys). The read-only experiment: cross-correlate Wikipedia attention avalanches with publicly published downstream behavioral datasets at different lags, looking for the transfer function between pond surface and dark-matter interior. The lag structure between the Wikipedia spike and the downstream behavioral shift measures how far the event penetrated below the membrane. An event that spikes pageviews but shows zero downstream behavioral correlation was surface noise — dark matter never coupled. An event with strong lagged correlation reached the tides. This does not require any live perturbation; all data sources are already public, read-only, and archivable.

THE PHASE-INVERSION PROBE FOR MEANING-SELECTIVE GAIN: At rung=6h, the wiki pond's persistence inverts — the circadian node creates anti-correlation. This is a structural property of a 24h periodic signal. But B6 (meaning-selective gain) predicts that certain CONTENT types would resist this phase inversion — specifically, content that is emotionally urgent enough to override the body's circadian damping. A person who would normally be asleep at 3am will stay awake if they are reading about a personal crisis or a breaking catastrophic event. The prediction: during genuine breaking-news events (earthquakes, political crises), the circadian anti-correlation at lag=6h should be WEAKER — the event energy overrides the circadian damping. The measurement: take the rolling 6h anti-correlation coefficient (already computable from the P-L4 data infrastructure), and correlate its time-varying value with the occurrence of known breaking-news events identified by the canon-radius instrument (windows where all 5 language ponds simultaneously spike). During global-canon events, the 6h anti-correlation should flatten toward zero. This is a read-only probe using data already collected, requiring only a time-series of the 6h autocorrelation rather than its 93-day aggregate. It would be the first direct measurement of meaning-selective gain as a suppression of a structural physical signal — not merely amplitude amplification but PHASE STRUCTURE DISRUPTION BY CONTENT.

THE TEMPORAL HOLOGRAPHY PROBE (B5 APPLIED): B5 claims that in the latent domain a single fine-scale sample carries information about the slow structure — the tide is readable from one ripple. The P-L3 probe was proposed in LATENT_CROSS_RUNG_SKETCH but not run. The aggressive version: take single Wikipedia article revisions from known historical periods (one revision per article, selected blindly from the edit history) and ask how many bits about the DECADE of the revision a compression-based stylometric model can extract from that single revision. Crucially, the same probe applied to the ATTENTION AVALANCHE DATA from P-L5 would ask: how many bits about the TYPE of event (political crisis vs. sports event vs. scientific discovery vs. celebrity death) does a single article's spike SHAPE (duration, peak/trough ratio, return-to-baseline curve) carry? If the avalanche shape is article-type-diagnostic, then the spike is a holographic readout of the event's semantic category — the wave's shape carries the meaning signature. This would be the first direct measurement of B5 (one ripple dates the tide) applied not to text but to BEHAVIORAL TIME SERIES, and it would quantify exactly how much semantic information survives in the aggregate attention signal that the probes assume is content-agnostic.

attacks.target: P-L4: circadian lines and timezone phases as non-trivial wrapper-layer readings
attacks.detail: The trivial portion reverses cleanly: phase offsets (en=19h UTC, ja=8h, de=15h, ar=18h, es=20h) are exact demographic timezone readouts. The ja -8h offset is literal JST, de -1h is literal CET. Peak/trough ratios rank by geographic concentration (de=9.63, ja=5.44, en=1.61), exactly as a demographics model predicts. No framework concept is needed: a population-weighted timezone histogram produces these numbers. The canonical 'wrapper-layer reading' framing earns nothing over the plain statement 'ja.wikipedia is used mostly in Japan, which is UTC+9.' HOWEVER: one non-trivial structure survives. The autocorrelation ladder (confirmed by rerunning on the raw cache: lag=1h rho=0.930, lag=6h rho=-0.009, lag=12h rho=-0.743, lag=24h rho=0.940, lag=168h rho=0.946) is genuinely non-monotone, and the 168h rho exceeding the 24h rho (0.946 > 0.930) is a real spectral line on top of the circadian, not a demographic artifact. This matches the Q6 rung-instrument framing: different causal laws at different rungs. The Q6 identity holds with RMS error 0.053 bits across 4 rungs, confirming the mechanism transfers from GOES flux to this pond. That is non-trivial and survives. The canon-radius claim is the core casualty. After detrending, deweeklying, and AR1-whitening the daily series, the residual correlation matrix collapses: mean off-diagonal drops from 0.385 to 0.176. The strongest surviving pair is de-es (r=0.425, t=3.15), the only one unambiguously non-zero at SE=0.145 (n_eff~65). The claimed 'Western canon bloc' (en-de-es strong, ja/ar weak) does not materialise: en-es residual is only 0.189 (t=1.30, indistinguishable from zero), while de-ar is 0.306. A timezone-similarity null (circular peak-hour distance) correlates r=0.534 with the residual matrix, meaning roughly half of the residual structure is still timezone, not content. Critically: zero global-canon events were found in the 93-day window (confirmed in skeptic_verdict.json: global_events_count=0), so the headline canon-radius claim ('global events correlate, local events diverge') is untestable as operationalized -- there are no positive instances.

The heavy tail is real and robust. The full 240-EN + 120-JA run (confirmed from p_l5_results.json: 2456 EN avalanches, 2082 JA avalanches) gives alpha=1.776 (EN) and 1.794 (JA) with CI95 [1.706, 1.844] and [1.734, 1.936]. The sensitivity grid spans 18 operationalization cells (threshold x baseline-window x gap) and alpha ranges [1.626, 1.811] for EN -- all cells alpha<2, confirming infinite-variance regime. The tail is real: p99=844x baseline (EN), R_max=17155x, and the qualitative conclusion (heavy tail, alpha~1.8) is robust. Sampling bias (top-K union) truncates the small end but not the tail that was fitted; the selection is disclosed and the tail estimates are on the tail. These findings survive. What reverses is the 'criticality-tuned' claim. Four separate tests fail it: (1) Vuong PL vs LN: p=0.666 (EN) -- power law and lognormal are statistically indistinguishable. delta_ll = -0.0001, essentially tied. A 'critical regime' should favour PL over LN decisively. (2) Burstiness BP=-0.037 (EN) and -0.035 (JA) -- both NEGATIVE, meaning inter-avalanche intervals are more regular than Poisson. A genuinely self-organized critical system generates bursty inter-event times (BP>0). Near-zero or negative BP means avalanche initiations are externally seeded on roughly independent scheduling, not internally cascading. The q90/q50 statistic (EN=3.30 vs Poisson null=3.32) is indistinguishable from an exponential inter-arrival distribution -- no bursty excess whatsoever. (3) Hurst H=0.33 (EN), 0.20 (JA), both < 0.5: spikes are anti-persistent (mean-reverting), not characteristic of a self-amplifying critical cascade. (4) SOC criticality requires simultaneous scaling across multiple observables (avalanche size, duration, inter-event times) with a consistent exponent family. Only avalanche size was tested; duration and inter-event time exponents are absent. 'Criticality-tuned' is a buzzword applied to a heavy tail that fails the decisive burstiness test and cannot be distinguished from lognormal.

attacks.target: P-L6: endogeneity handling and intervention-as-circuit-breaker claim
attacks.detail: The statistical association is real and survives: matched pairs (n=311) show mean delta_lambda = +0.025/d (CI [0.009, 0.041], p_signflip=0.003). The effect is present across three alternative matching schemes (caliper 0.25: p=0.004; nearest-1 control: p=0.017; protection-anchored window: p=0.001). This is not noise. What reverses is the causal interpretation as a 'circuit breaker on the attention ocean.' Three independent lines from the data break it. First, mechanism mismatch: the protection log shows zero protections triggered by traffic surge. The trigger census (arbitration 18%, vandalism 16%, disruptive 15%, sock 8%) is entirely editor-conduct-driven. Edit-protection blocks editors, not readers. Pageview decay is driven by the news half-life of the underlying event, not by edit friction. The matched control arm (unprotected articles with equal peak magnitude and pre-peak growth rate) decays more slowly -- but this is the arm without editorial conflict, not without external event. Second, lag structure: 50% of treated articles are protected on or before peak day (22% before peak, 28% on peak day). For the pre-peak protected articles, the surge occurred into an already-protected state. The decay difference in those pairs is not 'protection damped the wave'; it is 'articles under pre-existing community scrutiny have different post-event dynamics than uncontested articles of equal size.' Third, the EC stratum reversal (n=41, delta_lambda = -0.015): extended-confirmed protection shows the treated arm decaying SLOWER than control. EC articles are the most prominent, most community-watched articles. The reversal is consistent with protection signalling prestige/salience, sustaining attention via the editorial community and external linkers. This is the opposite direction of 'circuit breaker.' The aggregate positive delta_lambda is driven entirely by the semi-protection stratum (n=265, delta=+0.031), which is also the stratum with the most ambiguous triggering (vandalism+disruptive). The DiD trajectory is also non-monotone (reverses at days 2-5), inconsistent with a clean intervention effect. The most parsimonious explanation for the aggregate result: protected articles are systematically more topically volatile (that is why they attract both vandalism and high traffic), and matching on peak magnitude and growth rate does not fully control for topic-class volatility. The lambda difference is a selection residual, not a causal damping signal.

attacks.target: Anchor thesis operationalization: wrapper coupling coefficients vs relabeled correlations
attacks.detail: The anchor thesis claims the wrapper-stack coupling coefficients can be estimated from cross-pond correlations. Running the full skeptic analysis on the actual data shows this claim does not survive as operationalized. The cross-pond daily Pearson r (raw: en-es=0.686, de-es=0.694) drops to residual r (after detrend, deweekly, AR1-whitening: en-es=0.169, de-es=0.425) with 62-76% of the signal absorbed by shared weekly/monthly structure for most pairs. Only de-es survives as unambiguously non-zero (t=3.15). The timezone-similarity null (circular hour-offset metric) correlates r=0.534 with the residual matrix, accounting for roughly a third of its variance. The strongest anomaly -- de-ar residual r=0.306, despite tz_sim=0.750 -- is neither predicted by the wrapper-distance model nor by a simple timezone model; it is a weak observation that is statistically fragile at SE=0.145. The operationalization fails four tests: (i) the key observable ('wrapper coupling coefficient') has no definition that distinguishes it from Pearson r on daily volumes; (ii) the available data (daily aggregate views) cannot see which articles are co-spiked across ponds, so content-level coupling is invisible; (iii) zero global-canon events were identified in the 93-day window, making the event-study arm of the thesis untestable; (iv) no pre-registered wrapper-distance metric exists to allow an out-of-sample prediction test. The residual correlation matrix is a correlogram, not a coupling-coefficient measurement. Making the thesis falsifiable requires: (a) a registered article-level cross-language concordance instrument (for each EN spike, does the cognate JA/DE article spike within 48h?), (b) a wrapper-distance metric derived from the framework's own structure (e.g., geographic-linguistic overlap index), and (c) a directional prediction tested out of sample. None of these were done. The claim that 'wrapper layer readings' explain the correlation structure is unfalsifiable as currently operationalized and should be demoted to a working hypothesis pending the article-level instrument.

adversary.strongest_surviving_critique: The strongest surviving critique is the anchor thesis operationalization failure on P-L4. After removing shared weekly/monthly structure and AR1-autocorrelation from the cross-pond daily correlations, only one pair (de-es, t=3.15) is unambiguously non-zero out of ten. The claimed 'Western canon bloc' (en-de-es co-moving, ja-ar isolated) does not appear in the residual matrix: en-es residual is 0.189 (t=1.30, indistinguishable from zero), de-ar is stronger than en-ja. A timezone-similarity null correlates r=0.534 with the residual matrix, meaning the residual structure is still approximately half demographic. Zero global-canon events were identified in the 93-day window, so the event-study arm of the canon-radius hypothesis has no positive instances. The 'wrapper coupling coefficient' has no operational definition distinguishing it from a Pearson r on daily totals that cannot see which articles co-spike across ponds. The thesis is unfalsifiable in its current form: it makes no prediction that distinguishes 'content-level coupling through language wrapper' from 'shared European working-hours create same-day volatility in de and es.' This critique is not a minor methodological quibble -- it goes to whether the framework concept of 'wrapper coupling' can be measured at all with aggregate data, and the answer from the actual numbers is no.
