DIAL PLACEMENT vs Q6 FLARE AND REFERENCE SERIES

The Q6 flare (GOES X-ray, 1-min cadence) had: rho1@1min=0.996, edge=0 crossover at rung=60min (rho=0.484). The en.wikipedia pond at rung=1h already has rho1=0.925 — it enters the rung ladder at high persistence and decays non-monotonically due to its two-timescale structure. The wiki pond is MORE persistent at its native hourly rung than the flare is at its edge=0 crossover rung. It also has structure the flare lacks: a second resurgent memory at rung=168h (institutional weekly cycle). The flare was single-timescale (monotone rho decay); the wiki pond is a coupled two-process system. Cross-scale inference (B(r→r')) applies differently: the flare's rho-identity held with RMS 0.006 bits; the wiki's identity holds with RMS 0.053 bits, with the 6h node and 168h resurgence as the systematic deviations.

Circadian amplitude trend (testing Crokidakis 2026 gradual-degradation): Mar=FFT@24h 0.557 / Apr=0.555 / May-Jun=0.568 — no monotonic shrinkage over 93 days. Crokidakis prediction NOT supported on this timescale.

AVALANCHE CENSUS VERDICT (P-L5, 240 EN + 120 JA articles, 2025-06-01 to 2026-06-10)

Tail shape: power-law-compatible, alpha=1.776 EN / 1.794 JA, CI95=[1.706,1.844]/[1.734,1.936]. Alpha<2 = infinite-variance regime in both languages and across all 18 operationalization cells (threshold x baseline-window x gap). Sensitivity range: 0.185 (EN) and 0.128 (JA) — qualitative conclusion (heavy tail, alpha~1.7–1.9) is robust. R_max=17,155x EN / 9,892x JA. The tail is real.

Stochastic marginality (Okamura 2026 design change applied): Var[ln v(t)] grows proportional to ln(t), AIC wins over power model by 7.0 (EN) / 2.6 (JA). H_median = 0.33 EN / 0.21 JA, both < 0.5 (anti-persistent, mean-reverting after spikes). EN H=0.33 matches Okamura's ensemble estimate of ~0.32 — cross-validation of the instrument. Variance-growth slope b=0.60 (EN) vs 0.25 (JA): EN trajectories are 2.4x more uncertain after a spike.

Exogenous vs endogenous: BP = -0.037 (EN) / -0.035 (JA), both negative (inter-avalanche intervals slightly more regular than Poisson). A genuinely self-organized-critical system produces BP>0. The near-zero/negative BP means avalanche initiations are externally seeded (news events, viral shares), not internally self-sustaining. The pond amplifies external shocks to extreme amplitude but does not spontaneously chain avalanches from ambient noise.

Criticality-tuner claim verdict: PARTIAL — the heavy tail is real and survives the sensitivity sweep. But the SOC/criticality framing fails four tests: (1) Vuong PL vs LN p=0.666 — indistinguishable; (2) BP~0 — exogenous seeding not bursty cascades; (3) H<0.5 — anti-persistent, not self-amplifying; (4) only avalanche size was measured, not duration and inter-event time exponents simultaneously. The correct frame is stochastic marginality (Okamura 2026), not a tunable SOC exponent.

Language comparison: alpha is indistinguishable across languages (1.776 vs 1.794), but H differs substantially (EN 0.33 vs JA 0.21). JA spikes mean-revert faster/harder. Variance-growth slope 0.60 vs 0.25: EN shows much greater post-spike trajectory uncertainty. Consistent with EN being more deeply embedded in global recommendation traffic and JA more locally bounded.

Temporal drift: H1 alpha (Jun–Dec 2025) ~2.15 vs H2 alpha (Dec 2025–Jun 2026) ~1.66 across both languages — apparent tail-heavying trend, but confounded by sampling design (top-days only sampled from H2 period; H1-only articles absent from corpus). Cannot separate secular drift from selection artifact without a temporally uniform sampling design.

INTERVENTION DAMPING VERDICT (P-L6, 311 matched pairs, en.wikipedia, 2026-03-01 to 2026-05-10)

The statistical association is real and robust: matched pairs show mean delta_lambda = +0.025/d [0.009, 0.041], p_signflip=0.003. Effect survives three alternative matching schemes (caliper 0.25: p=0.004; nearest-1 control: p=0.017; protection-anchored window n=189: delta_lambda=+0.035/d, p=0.001). Same-weekday residual: d_lnR7=-0.310 [-0.472, -0.141], p=0.0003; DiD gap at k=21: -0.506 [-0.752, -0.261]. The association is not noise.

The causal 'circuit breaker' interpretation is challenged on three independent lines from the data itself: (1) Mechanism mismatch — zero protection events were triggered by traffic surge; triggers are editorial-conduct-driven (arbitration 18%, vandalism 16%, disruptive 15%). Edit-protection blocks editors, not readers. The pageview decay is driven by news-event half-life, and the matched control arm (unprotected articles with equal peak) decays more slowly because it lacks pre-existing editorial conflict, not because it lacks external event. (2) Lag structure — 50% of treated articles are protected on or before peak day (22% before peak, 28% on peak day); the surge occurred into an already-protected state, so the decay difference reflects community-scrutiny dynamics, not protection dampening the wave. (3) EC stratum reversal — extended-confirmed protection (n=41) shows delta_lambda = -0.015 (treated decays SLOWER than control), consistent with protection broadcasting a prestige/salience signal that sustains attention. The aggregate positive delta_lambda is driven entirely by the semi-protection stratum (n=265, delta=+0.031). The most parsimonious explanation for the aggregate: protected articles are systematically more topically volatile (that is why they attract both vandalism and high traffic), and matching on peak magnitude and growth rate does not fully control for topic-class volatility. The lambda difference is a selection residual plus a meaning-signal effect (protection status itself changes the article's social valence), not a clean causal damping signal.

The 43.4% of treated pairs where lambda_treated < lambda_control is not noise — it includes the Streisand-effect tails and the cases where protection extended the attention cycle. Streisand rebound rate: 0.96% treated vs 1.07% controls (rare in both arms, similar rates).
